purpose: The card-brand plate shown beside a payment card: a small bordered plate with the network's mark (Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Diners Club, JCB) drawn in theme tokens, so it reads in light, dark and forced colors without a raster image or a brand hex. It replaces the design sample's `CardBrandMark` (a Visa plate on a hard-coded blue fill), the Console Kit's `card-flag-block` (six colored SVG logos) and the inline Visa SVG the account blocks repeated. A brand it does not draw (Discover, Elo, Hipercard, UnionPay, or an unknown value) shows a generic card glyph and keeps the brand's name for assistive technology.
useWhen: A payment method row, a checkout summary or a billing table names the card on file: the plate sits before `Ending in 4242` or `Visa •••• 4242`.
A list of saved cards where the brand helps the reader tell them apart.
avoidWhen: A partner or integration logo (Git providers, clouds) → use the product's logo asset or an `Avatar`.
A status or category of the card (expired, default) → use `Tag` beside the plate.
related: brand` — the same idea for the Azion lockup: an inline mark, sized by token.
tag` — put `Default` or `Expired` next to the plate, not inside it.
bestPractices: Pass the brand as the payment API returns it; the plate normalizes `American Express`, `american_express`, `Diners Club` and casing.
When the row text already says the brand (`Visa •••• 4242`), set `decorative` so the name is not read twice; when the text says only `Ending in 4242`, leave the plate named.
Keep the plate at `medium` in rows and forms, `small` inside dense tables.
